utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? That would be --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Witness DP14 as far as I understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. I apologise that I can't see His Honour Judge Nieto-Navia. Just two matters. I think we still have the exhibits from the last witness to be tendered and secondly we have a technical problem on the Prosecution side. Because we have changed courtrooms we don't have on this system the LiveNote for previous days. Mr. President, I propose that we will live with that until such time as it becomes a problem for us. And if it is acceptable to you at that stage, I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have this same problem, Mr. Ierace. We only have a limited number of days on the LiveNote available to the court as well. If there would be any problem in respect of LiveNote or the transcript of one of the previous days, please inform me and we can see what we can do during the break, since some of us might have other LiveNote transcripts somewhere else in this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. At least if we can obtain the email connection, that should overcome our problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether an email connection could be established from here. Could we ask from the technicians...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed, Mr. Ierace, that in approximately 30 minutes you might have an email connection from the courtroom. Then, Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents still not admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1790, black and white copy of P3728, map marked by witness; D1788, under seal, pseudonym sheet; D1789, map marked by witness; D1724, daily sit-rep; D1713, daily sit-rep; P3755, black and white copy of map; and C2, the large map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. These documents are admitted into evidence. The pseudonym sheet under seal. If you are ready to call your next witness, then we first -- when the witness enters the courtroom, we will have to ask the usher to put the curtains down and as soon as the witness has taken his position, then they can be removed again. Mr. Usher, could you please. Yes. One moment, please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you please -- Mr. Witness, I'll not call you by your own name. I will call you Mr. DP14, since protective measures are in force in respect of you, that is, face alteration and pseudonym. Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The usher will now hand out the text of this declaration to you, and may I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Usher, could you raise the curtains again for the public gallery. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, before I am going to ask you certain questions, considering that you have been approved protective measures, I am going to ask you to look at the document so that you can confirm whether the data on this sheet is correct. Sir, Witness, did you have a look at the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. In the first letter of my last name there is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Everything else is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the problem lies in the impossibility to type the letter correctly, so I am going to correct this in closed session. Perhaps we can go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can, but then we have to -- Ms. Pilipovic, could we perhaps do it -- I take it it is just the first letter and I take it it is just a technical problem rather than a --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This courtroom is a bit different from the courtroom we are usually sitting in, Ms. Pilipovic. If we turn into private session, you can explain to us what the difference is and then it is not necessary to go into closed session. Can we turn into private session for just a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we are in open session again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you tell us in September 1992, where were you? Where did you live and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: In 1992 in September I was in Vogosca. At that time, I was the commander or commanding officer of the 3rd Company of the Krivolak Battalion. I did not work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, you are telling us that in September 1992 you were on the positions of the 3rd Company as the commanding officer of that company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when was this 3rd Company established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The 3rd Company was established at the end of August 1992. Initially it was a section of the company, but then because there was an influx of refugees from Visoko, Zenica and the surrounding area of Vares, there were many more people and therefore, that's how the company was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you tell us that until August 1992 it was a section, can you tell us whether you were a member of that section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Leaving Sarajevo on the 17th of April until 18th, 19th of May, until the wave of refugees arrived from Pofalici, I was in Reljevo. And then with the convoy of those refugees, I evacuated my wife and children to Sokolac at the end of May. 25th May to about the 1st of June I returned to Vogosca where my parents lived. I was then mobilised and I was tasked to that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP14. You told us that at the end of May you were positioned in this unit. Can you tell us about the manpower, the composition of that unit? Who was a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: At that time, at that time it was just the section, like a small platoon. There were 18 to 20 people, and mostly these were local people, inhabitants of that village or of that settlement. I was made commander, a commanding officer of that section or of that squad sometime in the beginning of June. First time at the Zuc and the first time when we were given area of responsibility about the 10th of June, at first these were just four trenches and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, we will come to that period, but I just want you to clarify the way that you were organised in your squad or in your section. How were you organised in that part of Vogosca as a municipality of the city of Sarajevo? How did you get organised, this squad or section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Since my parents lived there, from Sokolac, I returned to Vogosca. Because I already had, how shall we call it, a bad experience in Reljevo., where I used to live before, and wherever you don't know the people and if you are a refugee, the principle was to take a gun in your hands and you go into a trench. And in Reljevo, there were no trenches, but we would only patrol around the village at night, not during the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my co-counsel is telling me that the transcript isn't working. On my screen we only have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I agree with you that at this moment we do not receive any text on our screens. There seems to be a technical problem. It's running again now or not? So then we have to wait and see whether this could be repaired. I take it that we get a message from the technical booth as soon as it has been fixed. Two more minutes? Yes. The technicians will arrive and see whether it can be fixed quickly. Yes, we -- I do understand that we -- the problem has been fixed. Yes, then, Ms. Pilipovic, you -- the last words that appear in the transcript is that you asked -- you told Mr. DP14 that you would come to that period when he talked about the 10th of June, but that you just wanted to clarify the way the witness was organised "in his squad or in his..." That's where the transcript stops. Would you please start there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP14, if you don't mind telling us briefly, until the 10th of June, that is the end of May to the 10th of June, how were you organised? How was the squad or the municipality in Vogosca organised the squad that you belonged to, in which way were you organised? Can you just tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: When I returned to Sokolac to Vogosca to the village where my parents live, the people told me that I had to report to the Ministry of Defence which is what I did. And they just told me that I had to report to the command of the company, that is, of the battalion, and they told me to go to that place and join that squad. To start with, I was a private, a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14 do you know, since you are telling us that you joined this squad which later became part of that battalion, who were these people who made up this squad, and later on the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they lived and how was that squad organised? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Specifically there, I don't know. I know the people. I know they were locals. I know that they lived there before. How precisely they got organised I don't know because during that period, I was not in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the beginning you told us that in May, sometime in May, refugees arrived from Pofalici, Visoko and Zenica. Do you know anything about the refugees who came from Pofalici? Do you know why they came to that part of town, to the municipality of Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The refugees from Pofalici, I saw them in Reljevo. I think it was the 17th or the 18th of May, 1992. It was after the fight, after the offensive launched by the Muslims against Pofalici. I only saw women, children and elderly people as refugees who came from Pofalici to Zuc and took refuge in Reljevo. They came by bus. On the following days they were moved out to Sokolac by bus or taken to Sokolac by bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, if I understand you answer correctly, you are telling us that the population of Pofalici moved out of the town because of the Muslim attack; is that correct? Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14, just a minute ago you told us about Reljevo and Pofalici. Can you now tell us whether these places were parts of the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, they are and Vogosca and Ilijas and Hadzici and Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Pofalici and Reljevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, they were part of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14, when you told us that you were part of the 3rd Company which was previously the 1st Company and that your first task was in fact on the 10th of July 1992, have I understood you correctly -- on the 10th of June 1992 correction, have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. The first time on the Zuc hill, the first time I went to the Zuc hill it was then, after the enemy offensive which took place a few days prior to that date. And then a trench line was formed for the first time on the Zuc hill for the purpose of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, you are talking about the offensive against Zuc, which was carried out by whom exactly? Could you please be precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: By Muslim units. And when I went to Zuc I had the opportunity to experience those attacks in the following days. I saw the men who were attacking. They would cry out "Allah akbar. Allah is great." I saw that with my very own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, you are telling us about this Muslim offensive, the attack carried out by the Muslim Army. Can you tell us in the course of the fighting for Zuc, can you tell us what the positions were in Zuc, in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Zuc hill with regard to the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Without a map, it is difficult for me to do so. It ought to be to the south-west with regard -- in relation to the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence counsel will show part of the map to the witness. The number is 3724, and it is the second part of the map which shows, depicts part of the town of Sarajevo and the municipality of Vogosca. And this is so that the witness could clarify the matter of the positions of his company and the battalion by using this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet is bears the number 179, and then an "0" with an one through it. But since we have already 1790, it should be 1791. Therefore, this map cannot bear the same number. So I take it that it will then be D1792.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was following the transcript, and I think that it was the time for 1791. I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness DP14, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map the first area of the municipality of Vogosca? Can you first of all mark the area of the municipality of Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The area covered by the municipality of Vogosca, I don't know how -- I don't know what the surface was exactly, but I know the lines of defence in the municipality of Vogosca in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14, could you use a black felt tip to mark the lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The scale of the map is quite large, and it is difficult to draw the demarcation line in 1992 with precision.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, do carry on and then we'll address this later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: In this part here around Orahov Brijeg I don't think the map was put together very well. I don't think it was stuck together because there is a part which is missing, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the demarcation lines in relation to the other parts, in the other parts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: That's what it would look like from Motika [phoen], through Kremes on the other side of Ravne. But as I said, the scale of the map is large. So I can't find my bearings very well. And this part here from Kobilja Glava to Hotonj, I don't think this part can be seen very well, the part called Orahov Brijeg is missing, or rather in Donji Kotonj [as interpreted] Where the road passes through. Or the map is too old.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you mark the Zuc area on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Zuc is the area we called -- we called the area from Golo Brdo, the Zuc area. I can't see it from here, so the Zuc area extended from Golo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may briefly intervene. Perhaps it would be helpful to the Trial Chamber, or it would assist them if we can produce a slightly better map, in light of the fact that the witness has indicated that Orahov Brijeg is not visible on this map. That locality relates to three of the scheduled sniping incidents. Perhaps with your leave we could obtain a better map for the witness to use with respect to this area in light of the fact that we would anticipate, based on the 65 ter summaries, that the witness will be testifying about those very areas which he himself has indicated is not visible on the map, D1792.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There -- the witness testified that a part of the map was missing, and I see that there is some incongruence, especially, I would say, on the top of the map we go from 89 to 91. It seems that 90 is missing, perhaps a small portion. But would there be another map available of approximately the same size or could it be reproduced during the break? Because the -- if the witness says that parts of the map are missing and that's the reason why he can't draw the lines, then we should take that seriously.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But the Defence received this map from the Prosecution so we haven't had any problems so far up until now. We haven't had any problems so far with this map. So that what the witness said, given that he was there -- well, he is certainly more familiar with this than we are. I copied what I was provided with. Perhaps my colleagues have a more precise and better map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be some problem, because on the bottom of the map, number 89 is missing, however, on the top of the map, number 90 is missing, and I was just wondering -- on the other hand I see that there is some kind of an adjustment. I see a line from where it says "89" on the top, going down to where you would expect 89 to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not an expert in map reading, but could the Prosecution, if they have provided the map, assist. Do you see what the problem is?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it appears that the map D1792 is a photocopy of part of the same map which has been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 3274. P3274, on the map P3274, clearly the lines 88 through 92 are visible on both the top and bottom of that map. It would appear as though D1792, perhaps during the photocopying process, was folded. The map had previously been folded along the lines in the general vicinity of 89 and 90, and that perhaps could be why part of the area is missing on D1792. But clearly P3274 is or appears to be the source for map D1792. We do have -- my case manager informs me, we do have six copies of P3274 available and I am looking at this map, Mr. President, and it does not appear as though any witness has previously marked P3274. So I offer that, if that's of assistance to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I just have a look on the map you are referring to see whether the area which we are talking about and perhaps give a copy to the Defence as well so that we can check whether this would solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have just been informed by the case manager that apparently the mark -- the map that I have marked as P3274, in fact should be P3724.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the confusion we have had before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the Prosecution offers copies of 3724.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, with your permission I will show the witness this map so that he could mark the line with a greater precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. We will then use a map with the, at this moment, the erroneous marking with P3274 which should be 3724, and which will then get a "D" number later on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we should give it a "D" number then. If you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have marked D1791 on the map which is by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the wrong number. So it should have been D1792. And if you would not -- if you tender that one, we could perhaps call this one D1792.1 or .A, perhaps that's better, so that we know it is the same map, but especially in the area of Kobilja Glava is more precise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you mark the Kobilja Glava area on this map again, and the demarcation lines which you marked. And, first of all, is this map more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. In this map you can see the part that was missing in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. other one. The defence line has been marked here. This was in September. It was established on the 10th, the beginning of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, I think that you have marked the Zuc hill area on this map. It is not clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. Zuc was -- had quite a wide meaning for us. There was elevation 850 which we held until December 1992. There is the Orlic elevation, 876, which dominates in this area. We didn't hold this position. We never did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who held the Orlic position, number 876?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The Orlic elevation, and this area towards the town, was under the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know from which date they had this elevation under their control, number 876?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't in this area before the end of May, but I know that in Grahoviste was a Serbian village, and it was under the Serbs. Kuta which is on the map here. I am just telling you about the boundary villages. This was a Muslim village, it was under the Muslims. Below Jezevi there was a Serbian village which was held by the Serbs. Grahoviste, I don't know the exact date, but before Pofalici, there was a massacre there and between 10 and 20 people were killed. And on that occasion, only a few men remained there right up until the 10th of June when the Muslims launched an offensive a few days prior to that, and then in Grahoviste, the formation of this line remained. Twenty-four inhabitants from that area remained there at those lines. And inhabitants from other villages, but I don't really know the entire area of Zuc. Up to this day, not much is known, nothing is known about many people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP14, you are telling us that these lines were established during the fighting that took place, but in early June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. The first time I went there was the 10th of June 1992, and this is when I got to know this line, this position. My section held four trenches, exactly on the elevation point 850, and with the increase of the manpower of the unit, our area of responsibility got larger. And it was on the Zuc hill that the -- on the Zuc hill I was there. I was a witness there until the end of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14, on this map you also marked the positions of your battalion. Can you show that on the map? You told us that was Krivolak Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. It held the positions from about this cemetery until Kuta. In fact there is also an elevation point here. You can't see it on the map. I don't exactly know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you marked for us on this map the demarcation lines, that is the lines of defence, can you tell us which military formation held these lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: What I drew here is the line of defence of the Vogosca Brigade. And that's what it was like from the very beginning of the war until the end of 1992, until the December of that year, unchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you tell us that the map was unchanged until the end of December 1992, are you saying that this map, that is, the lines on the map after the December of 1992, did they change then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: They did change as far as Zuc is concerned. Mostly the changes took place in December after the offensive launched by the Muslims. And it was on the 9th of December that they took the elevation point 850. On the 13th of December they took Golo Brdo and elevation point 832 that we were at for the first time, at which we withdrew to after -- following the 9th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, on this map, could you please mark this area that you are saying that from December, from the Muslim offensive, that it did change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: This is the situation following the 9th of December. We held on to Golo Brdo. This is this point, as well as the elevation point 832, and from here to Vogosca it changed -- it stayed unchanged. Following several days from the 13th, the line went down here, more or less. Approximately, that's what it looked like and this is what the situation remained until June or July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you tell us that these lines that you've marked as the positions of the Vogosca Brigade, can you tell us the demarcation lines in relation to the positions of the BH Army, where were they and what was the distance between the lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May we ask Ms. Pilipovic for the sake of the transcript we first be a bit precise on what lines are drawn. The first line, indicating the positions before December 1992 up until December 1992, makes approximately a half circle around where it reads "Zuc" and 892. Then the first line, just north of it, in the direction of south-west ending to the right of the words "Perivoje," is the second line the witness has drawn. And the third line is also in the south-westerly direction just a bit north from the line I previously indicated which starts just south of the word "Kata" and goes through the words, "Perivoje" and is a bit longer than the other line. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you now show us on this map in relation to the positions of the Vogosca Brigade, can you mark the positions and the lines of the BH Army, if you know? If you can please use a dotted line to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, shortly after you finished describing, the witness added an additional line and I am wondering if that would perhaps be both clarified as to what that is and described for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please tell us what is the line you just marked which goes in an angle of approximately of 90 degrees of the line I previously indicated going in a north westerly direction just above the word Perivoje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This road that I drew is the extreme end, the very end of the area of responsibility of the Vogosca Brigade. It was my mistake that I drew the first line slightly longer. Further on, this was the area of responsibility of the Reljevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, for the transcript, Mr. DP, you are telling us that is above the letter "O", that's where the line continues, the area of responsibility of the Reljevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. Yes, this road that I drew, that I drew this line is the border of the area of responsibility between the two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that this is now clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, I only now noticed that the word "Perivoje" appears twice quite close to each other when I referred to that word, it was the word closest to what appears to be a village, rather than a mountainous area. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, so my question was whether on this map you could mark for us by using a dotted line and a black fine liner, the front lines of the BH Army in relation to the positions of the Vogosca Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: That's a very hard thing to do on this kind of map, the map of this scale. The demarcation lines were somewhere only 20, 30 metre apart. That is the very front lines, the first demarcation lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the first front lines, demarcation lines" what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Their trenches, their very first trenches on the line, sometimes there were only 20 metres away from our lines, in some places.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14 on this map, specifically in the area of Kobilja Glava, Gornji Hotonj, Slatine, and Brijeg, could you please mark the positions of the BH Army and of the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: This here I think is the transport faculty, one of the strongholds Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. throughout the war. Naturally, this here are the front lines, the direct demarcation lines. But on all elevation points, depthwise, there were stronger weapons. Now in this area, I am saying there is an area above the faculty called Glavica and on this map you cannot see it, but it was approximately here very near our positions. So it would be like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, as you are marking these positions for us, can you tell us if these were the positions which were such in 1992, 1993, through to 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: What is marked here now, the situation on the map, with very slight corrections, that is, in 1993 in July we returned to this middle line. Until the end of the war, that was the line that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, you tell us in this area that you have marked for us as the demarcation lines, how familiar are you with this area, you, personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: From the end of 1992 until July 1993, I worked as an operations officer only in charge of gathering intelligence information in the Vogosca Brigade. And at that time - as I say, it's been some years now, so I can't remember absolutely everything - but I did know a lot of information, a lot of data about distribution of Muslim forces, about the roads, about positions, about artillery positions. I had a monitoring section. I also had infrared equipment for night -- nocturnal observation. I did it for six months. I did this job for six months.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, I will ask you to the period from June 1993 to July 1993 when you say you were an intelligence commander officer in the Vogosca Brigade. Can you tell us on the basis of your observations of the positions, do you know what were the artillery positions of the BH Army, considering that you said that you knew about heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that they mostly had maneuvering weapons, that is, the weapons were frequently changed, their positions were changed, whether they were mortars mounted on lorries, I don't know which way they did it. It is not something that I actually saw ever. But I know that from many different places they fired from rubbish dumps, below Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you mark for us these locations that you mentioned. You told us a rubbish dump in Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. This is Hum. I have forgotten how you are supposed to draw certain symbols, but here from this location, there was frequent firing of mortars, and occasionally some tank vehicles -- some armoured vehicles, either a tank or something similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "mortars" can you tell us which calibre they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I am not an expert. There were many shells that were fired that landed around me. Hundreds of them landing on the positions, depth of my brigade. There were 60-millimetre calibre, and 120-millimetre calibre mortars, mostly from talking to other people who knew and told me which calibre it was. Personally I never saw or I never studied from which shell or which grenade, the crater was -- which crater was caused by which shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP14.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Honour, that it is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, usually we have a break after one hour and a half, and we are now still some 10 minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... when we start in the morning, so I have a full understanding of this small mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My colleague tells me that in the transcript there is a mistake, so I am going to ask Mr. DP14 again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the mortars, can you tell us which calibres they were? Can you please repeat which calibres they fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: They fired from all calibres. I am not an expert. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "all" --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: From 60 to 120. So 60-millimetre, 82-millimetre and 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP14, when you told us about the period from 1992 until the end of 1993, and you told us about the heavy weapons positions that the BH Army used, can you tell us in this period was there fighting in this area? And we are talking about Kobilja Glava, Slatine, Gornji Hotonj areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I am sorry, which period?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The end of 1992, July 1993. You told us that during this period you were an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think it is very hard during this period to find one single day. I don't think that there was a single day that there was no shooting. There were either shells or infantry weapons or I suppose a person would have to look in a diary and be specific. But there was daily shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you say that there was fighting, at the end of 1992, as far as you know, and you were in this area, were there any offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Throughout December 1992 there was the operation on Zuc was underway starting, I think, about the 5th of December. That was the first time that we lost a position, a line, which was a little bit in front of elevation point 850, some 5 to 600 metres in front of that elevation point. On the 9th of December we lost the elevation point 850. On the 13th we lost the elevation point 832. On the 22nd, 23rd, I was slightly wounded. On the 13th I was slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter is not quite sure when the witness was wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that that was the last -- the latest offensive. There was the offensive on Kuta elevation point. But there is another elevation point that we called Jezevi and that is where the very last defence of Vogosca took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you are telling us about the fighting in December in this area, can you tell us whether the fighting that you call "daily fighting," was this reflected on the wider area of Sarajevo as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Of course. Particularly after the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade was established where I was also an operations officer, I know that there was a joint operation and that if there is an offensive ongoing on one part of the city, it would be -- it is then normal that on the other side of town there would then be, if not an offensive, then at least there would be some operations so that -- so that wherever there was a lot of pressure it would be taken off.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, since you were an intelligence officer in the Vogosca Brigade until the end of July 1993, can you tell us whether in this period that is until you were in the Vogosca Brigade, in that period in 1993, were there any offensive operations that were of such proportions that they also encompassed wider areas of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: June, July, August in 1993, our offensive was launched, and it was underway. This was Operation Lukavac 1993. At that time we attempted, that is my brigade was attacking on the elevation point 850 Orlic, and we tried to break that. And we didn't succeed. The offensive lasted two or three months. I know from stories, from what people told me, that this was much wider. But I was in Zuc, I was on Zuc hill, so I know that part very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP14, you're telling us that in July and August 1993 in this area, that is, in Zuc area and on the positions of the front line of the Vogosca Brigade as you have marked them, that in that period there was fighting between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: In this part, in this area, demarcation line was between 20 and 50 metres distance. There was not a day that passed without some shooting, some grenade falling. I think that these days without any shooting simply didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you tell us, you told us, perhaps you can correct me, at the end of June, July 1993, you were an intelligence officer in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Vogosca Brigade. What was your position after that in the Vogosca Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I told you that in the first half of 1993, I was an operations officer, that I was in charge of intelligence data in the Vogosca Brigade. Before the Lukavac 1993 operation, the Tactical Group Vogosca was created, and then I was the operations officer at the TG Vogosca until the 3rd Sarajevo Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, when you say "TG Vogosca" could you tell us what "TG Vogosca" mean, and speaking from an establishment point of view, what did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It is a tactical group, Vogosca and it consisted of a group of brigades or I should say parts of brigades that were involved in the Lukavac 1993 operation in the wider area from Miljacka, in fact from Rajlovac, up to Mrkovici. So that would be from the Vogosca side towards the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us about the fighting in this area and you told us that it was practically on a daily basis, can you tell us from -- which weapons were used by both sides? You tell us briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: All available weapons, mortars from 60 to 120-millimetre calibre, armoured -- armoured weapons. In the Vogosca Brigade we had one tank. I know because I saw it with my own eyes. On the 5th of December I saw enemy tank on the elevation point 850. I saw an enemy tank. Perhaps it is not logical, but that's what happened. In 1993 when we took Golo Brdo in the attack, also one tank took part in the fighting and it stayed in front of our lines on fire. There were mortars. I have already mentioned from Smetljiste, from the rubbish dump from 1992 and there was frequent firing from a tank or some armoured vehicle, and it fired from the area of Kosevo hill or from those tunnels down there. At the city cemetery at that time I thought, according to the information I received, I thought that's where the mortars were located. And then in Dumaca I think on this map you cannot see it but it should be somewhere around here. That's where the mortars were located. I have already told you about Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, so that we are clear about this, you've just marked with a line, can you please mark -- put number "1." You told us above number 624, that's where mortars were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Here in Dumaca, there were mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, now it is approximately 90 minutes after we started. If you could find a suitable moment for a break soon, we'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP14, can you tell us this line which goes above this 624 elevation point where you have marked the mortars, what does this line mean? It actually goes above here. Is this some kind of a road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: You mean this line here? That is a regional road or a local road, regional road Sarajevo to Vogosca. It is an asphalt road, the only road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps before we have a break, could I ask one clarification from the witness. Just an answer it was not clear to me, that's why I am asking you. You told us that if there was an offensive ongoing on one part of the city, then at least some operations would be on the other side of the town so that wherever there was a lot of pressure it would be taken off. Were you referring to an offensive ongoing from the -- first one, from what armed forces? From the Muslim forces? From the BiH forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Muslim forces are attacking Zuc, it will be normal or it was normal to expect that, for instance, Kosevo Brigade, that is, our forces, if not launching actual attacks, they would then actually pretend that they were launching attacks so in order to take pressure off of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I did understand you well when you were talking about the offensive which would be followed by operations elsewhere, that the offensive you were talking about the opposite armed forces and the operations in another area would be your operations. Is that a correct understanding of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. But for instance, if we were carrying out an operation in one part, it would be normal that they would be pretending in other parts of the city. The same thing was done by the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say the other party would behave similarly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. We will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague will continue to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good day. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you answer my questions by saying yes or no, to the extent that this is possible. You spoke to us a minute ago about shots, about mortar shells of all calibres. Did you see any craters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see them very often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see them in all terrains, on all sorts of terrain, and in particular in asphalt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And did you see craters caused by shells of various calibres in asphalt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And as a result did you see, and if yes, how often did you see them? Did you see craters caused by 120-millimetre shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think that in 1993 in Vogosca, I think it was then, I think that that is the calibre of mortar shells that they used, but naturally I can't be 100 per cent sure because this is what I was told by others. They told me that this was the calibre that was used, but I was at the site where these shells would fall --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that you were at the site. Could you tell me what site that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: That was at the very crossroads in the vicinity of the medical centre. It was on the other side of the medical centre, there was the market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects and draws to the attention of the Trial Chamber the witness's testimony on page 22, lines 2 through 10, from earlier this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you -- I take it that you have found the source indicated by the Defence [sic] --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I don't really see what the objection is founded on, what the objection consists of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the Prosecution was pointing to this part of the testimony in order to draw your attention to the limits contained in those answers as to the source of knowledge. And looking at the line, page 29, line 22, we find this confirmed. So would you please keep this in mind when continuing your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my question related to the site. I don't see that this objection can be maintained. My question related to the site. Is the objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last question was about the site --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I understand this objection to be against the line of questioning which was initially not just related to the site; is that correct, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. My learned colleague began with a series of leading question to which we did not object. However based on the witness's previous testimony which I highlighted just a moment ago, we would object on the grounds of lack of foundation, source of the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please keep that in mind and please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you were present when there was shelling. You told us about the main crossroads, about the medical centre and about a market. What can you tell us about these various locations in Vogosca, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't understand you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that you saw craters in the vicinity of these locations. Are -- you told us that you were in the vicinity of these locations when there was shelling in course; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What was there in the vicinity of these locations which could have justified the shelling of the town, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The brigade command, for a certain period of time, was located in the primary school in the vicinity of that crossroads. It was perhaps 150 metres away. The battalion command for the entire period was in the building of the nursery school which is perhaps 2 or 300 metres from that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned a market. Was there anything near this market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, I said that those shells fell at the crossroads, at the main -- on the main crossroads in Vogosca. And then in the immediate vicinity you had the medical centre and the market behind the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would now like to show you an exhibit, 1793, D1793.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could assist us, please. I would be grateful if you could provide a coloured copy. I will take advantage of this time to ask the witness other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know what a Dragonov is; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, were there what we call snipers in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: There were 153 men in my company. There wasn't a single sniper in that company. There never was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you have a map which we are going to put on the ELMO and we should be able to see it on the screen, too. It's to your right. Thank you. Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. To the north you can see the positions of the VRS Army and to the south you can see the positions of the enemy. Does this line seem exact to you; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: They are not completely exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. May I continue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: To the extent that these lines are not correct, could you correct them from memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you take a black felt tip and proceed. If this line has to be corrected, could we start from the VRS position, if it has to be corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Marks] As far as the Republika Srpska Army, there is only this change that has to be made, but we were in -- at the elevation 703 in the vicinity, but this area that I am pointing to now is Orahov Brijeg, Orahov hill. Without a military map it is difficult to show the exact location, the exact line. This black feature here, this Betanija, it was held by the Muslim forces throughout the war. It was an important stronghold for them here. If --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the areas in which the witness is describing could be described for the benefit of the transcript or perhaps marked by the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the black feature just in the middle of the map, that seems to me that that is the really only black feature. Yes, but it could be mark if necessary, but I think it would be sufficient to refer to as the black area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the area which the witness described as Orahov Brijeg could be also be described or marked on the map please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If my recollection was well, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that was above the number"4" a little bit left and above the number "4" and between the lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I would have liked the witness to comply, first of all, and then show the lines, and then we could carry on, if necessary. I think that the lines, what is important, and then we will see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would be grateful if you could draw the lines, the BH lines at the time, and according to what you know. If you are not able to do so, that is no problem, no one will hold it against you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: As I said, this feature was always in the hands of the Muslims. It was an important stronghold and they were active from this site, they were constantly active from there. This is an asphalt road over Orahov Brijeg, and I think that this is the peak, somewhere around here. It is the elevation of Orahov Brijeg itself. If this is right, then the positions went -- the positions were below that point, so they were closer to our lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other changes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you take the pointer, please, with the assistance of the usher. My first question is as follows: A minute ago you said that not a day passed without an exchange of fire. In the zone that we have on the screen, was this the case? So your previous testimony that not a single day passed without an exchange of fire, does this previous testimony also apply to the zone that we have in front of us on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It applies, it refers to the entire zone of responsibility of the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when we speak of exchanges of fire, what sort of intensity are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. An exchange of fire could be sporadic, it could involve one shot or two shots or there could be several exchanges of bursts of fire or perhaps other heavy weapons might be used. So this is a quantitative question that I am putting to you. What can you tell us about these exchanges of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, let's say that I don't think there was a single day -- well, if we were to count this, it would be between 100-200 bullets. I don't fully understand, but it is very difficult --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I will interrupt you. If I am asking you the question for June, July and August 1993 would you -- would your answer be the same for this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: June, July and August 1993, that was the period of our operation, Lukavac 1993. And that period was certainly not, so to say, an average period. At that time, the intensity of the fighting was -- was great.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you please take the pointer and put it on the dark green line, the one which is most to the north.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you indicate in what direction the exchanges of fire took place, both for the dark line and for the light line. What were they shooting at from this line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I said that Orahov Brijeg was an important stronghold, and in the action in January 1993 we discovered that beneath the elevation, towards our lines, there were trenches which were beneath the asphalt. The trench came from this side. There were trenches which had been dug on the other side, and from this part, our positions came under fire, constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I apologise. From the line in the north, what were your objectives? What were you targeting? What were you shooting at, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the line to the north the witness drew a line which goes to the south, to a line in the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, does what you did apply to all the lines that we have on the screen; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, the Prosecution would ask that this be clarified with slightly more detail than "line to the south."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness was pointing from the outmost end on the left of the dark green line, approximately downwards on the map which, I take it, will be south. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what you have just done in the eastern part of this map, was the situation the same in the central and western parts? I apologise, you did it in the west. I apologise. What you did in the western part, was the situation the same in the central and eastern parts of the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I'll reformulate that. Could you put the pointer at the line -- on the line in the centre, the dark green line. Further to the right, further to the right. That's right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you indicate the direction of fire from that line, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you indicate that? Witness, please, put your pointer there. That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop. Witness, from a point which is below line 4, above line 4, traced a direction going south-west, south-west and south-east. Witness, if we do the same thing for the eastern part of the map, could you put your pointer further to the right now. A little further. That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the direction of fire here, exchanges of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed going towards the south-west and to show the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like you to do, could you please trace an imaginary line on this map between the red circle that you see right from your pointer, and the red dot which is to the south corresponding to number "4" can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you just explained for the transcript what the witness was pointing at, he was pointing at lines to the south --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you now pointed to the red circle. Do you see towards the south a red dot which is indicated by a number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since you interrupted me, my words do not appear in the transcript correctly. I said that the witness was pointing to the south-west from the last point you asked him, and to the south. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I had another interpretation in my ears. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, between these two points that you mentioned on the map we see slightly to the south of the circle an area which is represented by certain symbols. Could you please show -- no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, slightly higher. Could you go higher. South of the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you just go to the circle, please. On the red circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just below you see a symbol. Below, yes. That's right. Go a little bit below.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. This symbol, what is it? What does it mean in the field, on this terrain? What does it mean just below the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: This is a road and these are probably houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So the symbols are houses, but we can also see light green symbols. They seem like clouds. Now, they are certainly not clouds. What are they? Can you see them on the map? What are these symbols exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It's a wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke to us or you tell us about a wood. You mentioned on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how thick is this wood, what is it made of, what is the terrain in this area like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't remember that very well. But as the war progressed, it was increasingly damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So this wood, would this be an obstacle for fire, for shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: From our lines, from our trenches, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you. If, hypothetically, we put ourselves in the interior of the red circle, that is, above this wood would this wood represent an obstacle to hit the red dot and the number 4 that you can see below on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think that it is a great distance between these two points. As far as I remember it will be at least 1800 to 2.000 metres on the terrain in real life.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But, my question is the following: The wood that we see in symbols on the map, as far as you can recall would this wood represent a specific obstacle for a weapon being fired in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I cannot recall all those details, but in this area here there was an orchard, there were lots of fruit trees. So in principle, all of this here would be a very difficult terrain for observation. It was a difficult terrain for observation and for seeing targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has indicated with his pointer in the area close to the intersection of the lines on the spot, slightly to the right of the number "4" where he indicated that the entire area was covered by fruit trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you the question in relation to number 14. Can you find it? Dot number 14.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. The same question. Hypothetically, between the red circle and the point number 14, so both the wood and the fruit trees would be a direct obstacle for firing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know this road --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's an objectionable question, Mr. President. It is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I also your attention for the way you are reflecting the testimony -- the way you reflected the testimony before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... fruit trees. Your reflection of the words of the witness were not entirely correct, made it stronger. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what can you tell us in terms of field of vision, that is about the possibility or impossibility of a direct firing between the red circle and dot number 14, since in between there were partly the orchard, as you have said, and to the north of that, there was the wood that you told us about. What can you tell us about this, specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: The road on which point 14 is located, I observed it on many times. Because in Dumaca, there were mortars, and this was the main road for bringing ammunition supplies for these mortars. And also, for the units in Hotonj and Zuc. And I am saying that this road, this bit here, could be seen well. This is about a period of 1993. And this here below is possibly invisible in parts. And it is a huge distance, at least 2.000 metres from our positions to these points. We had this road as marked for targets, but for artillery weapons, particularly, because of its role, of the role that is played --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am not quite sure I saw it properly. I think your pointer was little too swift for me so I am not quite sure I managed it. Just a moment. Just a moment, Witness. The question I asked you was the following and can you please focus on the question that follows: Theoretically speaking, bearing in mind the features that you mentioned, an orchard to the south, wood for the upper part, hypothetically speaking, if there was a shot fired from the red circle and towards point number 14, the wood and the orchard would represent an obstacle. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think that the wood and the orchard above point 4 would not represent an obstacle, but between these two roads, there were also fruit trees. There were houses. So I think that that's almost impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was impossible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Impossible to fire at this distance any kind of target from infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Because of the distance; because of the greenery; because of the orchard; because of the houses that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, the same kind of problem. Can you see a number 9, a point number 9 on the map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What can you tell us, according to your experience, personal experience, what can you tell us about this point in relation to a hypothetical shot that would have been fired from the red circle, from within the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think the same applies for number 9 as it applies for point number 14. Because I spent a lot of time observing this road and this area. I think that it is almost impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in terms of instructions or orders on this subject, were there any instructions or orders given to you in your unit regarding the problem of the exchanges of fire or the necessary protection of civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Always, but particularly from the end of 1992 orders were strictly bear in mind the ammunition, the use of ammunition because there was less and less ammunition. So not to shoot at civilians, and not to shoot at any civilian facility. That was forbidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I'd like you to have a look at the piece that would be P3261. I just want to check whether this is not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We told Madam Registrar about this earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, we have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we need it on the ELMO, then we have to go into closed session. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, during that time, perhaps I could ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you have the opportunity to hear shooting or grenades being fired, grenade launchers being fired; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is it possible to hear a grenade -- a shell while it is falling, that is, while it is flying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. If it is falling within a radius of 100 metres around you. So only as it is falling, as it is going downwards, as it is falling down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the rest of the time, what would be your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It would depend on where it was fired from. It is possible to hear the actual firing. That depends on how far it would be from you, how far from you it would be fired, up to about a kilometre. I am not -- that's not something I can tell you precisely, I can tell you accurately. But the landing of the shell you can only hear if it falls within that radius.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am not talking about the moment when it is fired, but I am talking about the shell as it is flying, after it's been fired, before it falls. So some 100 metres that you are telling us about, is it possible to hear it then during that time in its trajectory during its flight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It can only be heard if it is falling in this radius around you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether we are -- can go now into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. The usher will draw up the curtains.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is map number C-2, I believe, according to what we have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the meantime, Witness, and while waiting to have a look at the map, as far as the material destruction of buildings are concerned, and I am talking generally in Sarajevo and as far as you know when did the damage occur for the most part? When did the most considerable part of the damage occur, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the war, April to June, July, August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And while we are talking about this, you talked about the high points of Zuc and the elevation point 876. Do you think you can tell us about -- more about other elevation points that were under the BH Army control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: On Zuc, elevation point is the most important is Orlic with its three parts. Then I also said Betanija, to us in Vogosca Brigade, it was a lot of trouble, it caused a lot of trouble for us. Then there was Balino Brdo, I think it would be a lot easier with a map, I think. And then the hillsides, or the slopes around Orlic, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you'll have a look at the map now. And please, could it be opened on the area that we are interested in which is the area around Vogosca, please, and Zuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please assist the usher who is -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, so have we got the right part on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if that is necessary, but I think that -- I think we are managing right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, while the usher is putting the map on the ELMO, we are close to the two hours, approximately two or three minutes still to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But I have three documents to show, to tender, and these other documents are here. And I can't go in another order. I have three other documents to tender later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The tendering of documents is part of the time used. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but we only have one usher, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking you how much time you would still need? I am not asking for a yes or a no answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten minutes maximum.
