utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, very quickly, I think that you can recognise this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could we concentrate on the northern part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the technical part focus on the northern part, please. Thank you. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the map that you have in front of it, does it correspond to the situation on the ground, yes or no, what could you tell us very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, the positions around Vogosca are not -- they don't quite correspond to the actual situation. This is probably a corps map. Our map in the brigade was always far more detailed, far more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove the map. We can remove it. We are now going to show a document, D1405, according to the number we have, and then it will be D1406, and then D1407, and we will hand these out altogether to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you will be shown these three documents, but first of all I would like you to have a look at them and tell us whether you have already seen such documents, this type of document while you were in active service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I saw such documents earlier on too, and I personally at the beginning of 1993 and at the end of 1992, I personally made such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I will stop you there to save time. Could we have a look at the first document, D1405, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this document mentions the existence of attacks carried out by 82 and 120-millimetre mortars. I would be grateful if you could tell us what other weapons the BH Army could have used, as far as you know, during that war? And I am referring to heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I have already said that during those days I saw a tank, I saw it with my very own eyes at elevation 850. There were mortar tanks, there were other artillery weapons, for example, Howitzers, multiple rocket launchers. It acted towards the end of December 1992, from the outside ring from the Nisic plateau plain from Ravni Nabozic and it fired on Vogosca. The multiple rocket launcher fired on Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever have the opportunity to see did you ever see ammunition fired from what you referred to as multiple rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes, and the place where they fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What can you tell us, if you can tell us anything, about the place of production of such ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1406. Document D1406, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the same question: Do you recognise this type of document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. We can see in this document that it mentions the presence of tanks. It is in the plural. You saw one tank. This document mentions several tanks. Do you know whether there were several tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I know that one was active from the tunnel in Ciglane and I know that one acted from Smetljiste and I know that one was involved in Hum where the repeater was. I saw this with my very own eyes at elevation 850. That doesn't mean that there weren't more of them and likewise it doesn't mean that there were 10. If they were mobile, and naturally they were, mobile. I don't know how many there were. This one is one that I saw with my very own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, document D1407 and my question is the same, do you recognise this type of document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, in the middle of the second paragraph it mentions enemy provocations. You worked for the secret service and what does enemy provocations mean? What sort of provocations are being referred to? What can you tell us about this? Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, provocations that meant staging attacks, infantry fire on part of a line, if it wasn't followed by some large-scale offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. But was this something that happened frequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning I said it was difficult to think of a day that passed without shooting. Sometimes the intensity was greater; sometimes it was not so great, but there was shooting almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you talk about fire are you also referring to heavy weapons or just small arms fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: This can only refer to small arms, infantry fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to show you with the assistance of the usher one last document, but this document refers to sniper units. Do you know whether there were any sniper units which were engaged against you at the time of the fighting in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Whether there were sniper units or not, it is difficult for me to say. I never saw a single sniper. But I also know that my comrade who was next to me died. He was hit by something that had the dimensions of 20 centimetres. He was hit in the forehead and I don't know whether this can be done with an ordinary weapon. He was hit from a firing hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just need to confer for 30 seconds, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about trenches a minute ago, did you see the trenches being dug; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What can you tell us about the people who, in your zone of responsibility, dug trenches on the side of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I know that after elevation 832 fell, I know that they were digging trenches in the direction of our forces and they were about 10 to 15 metres from our trenches. We fired at them with the artillery. We fired at those trenches. And when a shell would fall, after three minutes they would start digging again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I will stop you there. I was referring to the act of digging the trenches themselves, and this will, without a doubt, be my last question. Did you see trenches being dug, and if yes, what can you tell us about it? Who was involved in digging the trenches, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, that's what I want to say. If a shell fell, they wouldn't dig for three minutes, and then they would continue immediately. I think that the Serbs were involved in this. I think that Serbs were used to dig the trenches on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How do you know that? What is your source of information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, through conversations with colleagues, and after the war with colleagues, they were personally involved with that, conversations with Serbs after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said you were put the last question to the witness, it seemed to be not your last one because another one followed. You also told us that you certainly -- that you would not need more than ten minutes. These ten minutes were already over the time of the two hours indicated. So if there is one final question, I am talking about one final question, you may put it to the witness. Please proceed, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. My only question, and it was the same question, it was to know whether the witness could provide the names of these people, but perhaps we should go into private session but that might be too complicated. But if possible, this is the question that I would like to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that would be your last question. Would you be able, Mr. DP14, to give the names of those who gave you the information about who were involved in trenches digging at the other side of the confrontation line? Could you do so? If so, we will turn into closed session. You can then -- or perhaps private session would do as well. If you could give those names, please tell us so. If you are not able to do so, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People who were in the town, people with whom I spoke, there are quite a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question is whether you can give the names, not whether there were many but whether you can give the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I would like to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then turn into private session so the names that you are now mentioning will not be heard by anyone outside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in light of the time, I would respectfully request that we take the recess at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment. Yes, then that's perhaps a good idea. We will adjourn until 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the Chamber was informed that you wanted to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. At this stage I envisage that cross-examination will be by both Mr. Mundis and I. There are some issues I would seek to raise at this stage. Firstly, in relation to the examination-in-chief, we were provided with a list of exhibits which included 18 exhibits that were not shown to the witness. We were also informed that the witness would be giving evidence in relation to scheduled sniping incidents number 16 and 17 and we heard nothing of those. However, my main concern as it relates to cross-examination, is that during examination-in-chief this witness was asked for his -- there was a number of issues which were raised which require a decision in the first instance on the part of the Prosecution as to how we respond. And I would be grateful for some guidance from Your Honours as to what you require. The first of those issues was an estimate of distances that the Defence drew from this witness in relation to three incidents. In respect of scheduled sniping incident number 4, in the Prosecution case we led evidence that the distance was taken by Mr. Hinchliffe with a laser finder indicating a distance of 940 metres and I think the evidence from this witness was it was around 1.800 or 2.000 metres, whatever it was, it was certainly well in excess of that. And similarly, there was evidence drawn from this witness in relation to the other two incidents in the same area, and the witness, Mr. Hinchliffe, gave an approximation for Incident 14 of 1.100 metres, again, well below the estimate given by this witness. Now, if it is acceptable to Your Honours, I am happy to leave it at that, in other words, for Your Honours to consider the Prosecution evidence alongside the Defence evidence as to distance in due course. What's more troubling than that is the evidence led from this witness that in relation to incidents 4 and 9, and I think also 14, there were obstructions to the line of sight, namely, a wood and orchards. Your Honours may recall in the Prosecution case we showed in respect of each of those incidents 360 degree electronic photographs. And if one focuses on incident number 14, it is clear that there is a gully between the suspected source of fire and the position of the victim when he was shot. Now in order to rebut that evidence, I would have to take the witness to the electronic 360-degree photographs for the three incidents and lay the appropriate foundation with him in order to demonstrate that whether there was a wood or not whether there were orchards or not, in terms of the evidence as to the position of the victims and the suspected sources of fire, there was no obstruction. That would consume, I should think, at least an hour, possibly a couple of hours. Again provided that does not work against the Prosecution in due course, I am content to leave that to Your Honours to decide upon when Your Honours consider the appropriate verdicts and at that stage to review in your own time the relevant evidence from the Prosecution and consider it along side the evidence of the Defence. Mr. President, if you deem that it is not necessary for the Prosecution to do that, in particular in light of the fact that that Prosecution evidence was not challenged in relation to lines of sight in respect of the relevant sources of fire, then cross-examination for my part will be eliminated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes Mr. President. The Defence is surprised. Defence counsel tried to respect the limit that was indicated, the two-hour limit, and we decided not to mention certain other incidents, simply because we didn't have the time, and we didn't want to place ourselves in a situation in which your Trial Chamber had reason to tell us that we had passed beyond the limit that was acceptable. So we played along and now we are hearing the Prosecution say that they need, in fact, more time and yet again they are approaching us with not having allegedly contested, or as we should have done this at the time, we hadn't contested certain facts. We should remind you of this. This will be the last time. We always contested the existence of the possibility of a shot. We contested the photographs, on the basis of principle. It was a standing objection that we made. So we shouldn't be told that we had accepted these details, and we shouldn't be told that a rule imposed this or not, 90 bis(H) imposed certain things. If some things should be respected, this is your decision, according to which a tandem intergression should not be allowed, if one out of the tandem was not present during the entire examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there might be some misunderstanding. What Mr. Ierace expected you to do is to put to the Prosecution witness when they said the fire came from there to say there is no line of vision to the position of certain forces. I think there is some confusion as to challenging evidence in general terms, challenging that a situation ever existed in pre-trial briefs or in pre-defence briefs, or to put that to a witness who testifies on a specific issue, on a specific issue, a specific incident. I think there is still some misunderstanding on what would be the system. I think it is not at this very moment -- perhaps you should sit together and perhaps once try to understand how Mr. Ierace interprets what is the standard in this kind of adversarial system and perhaps you explain to him how this works differently, perhaps in a civil law tradition. That is just in order to create a better understanding. Then may I ask you one thing, Mr. Ierace: We heard quite some evidence from this witness on change of confrontation lines on Zuc hill and intensity of combat. Was that, in general, in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't directly answer the question whether it is in dispute, but I can say this: It is essentially irrelevant, what happened on Zuc, where the confrontation lines were on Zuc. I can also assist you by saying that the confrontation lines, the evidence of the confrontation lines that the witness gave in relation to the three scheduled incidents in the area of Kobilja Glava are consistent with the Prosecution evidence, including the change he made to the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So I don't know why the Defence took half an hour to go through confrontation lines around Zuc, but it is certainly of no great consequence to the Prosecution and we don't intend to cross-examine about that aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am asking you because it might guide the Defence to use its time as efficiently as possible. Because if there are certain issues that are not disputed by the Prosecution, and if it is in accordance with the testimony given by the Prosecution witnesses -- and I also still remember about the black feature in the middle of the page that the line was drawn a bit to the other side. If you say we played the game as we were expected to play it, then perhaps the priority in issues you would like to raise should not be with those issues where your witness does not contradict or does not challenge the evidence presented by the Prosecution because you might have more important issues. Then we come to two issues -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, I would like to briefly say this: If we have wasted time with this witness, it is for a very simple reason. We wanted to demonstrate before this Trial Chamber that he was perfectly familiar with the lines, and when we asked what the direction of fire was, when we asked the witness what the direction of fire was, he was able to indicate the direction very well. He knew the sites, exactly. He knew where the fire was directed. And I think it is clear for everyone that part of the Defence thesis is -- relates to stray bullets. And when he traced these lines, it is obvious what the direction of fire is. He knew this very well. And this is the reason for which we proceeded in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am not saying that there was no evidence that was new. I am just saying that those parts of the evidence which is entirely in conformity with the Prosecution witnesses that it, certainly, if you had other issues in your mind, then perhaps not touch these issues first. But let's -- we have two then main, remaining issues. The Prosecution seeks guidance as to whether to deal with the distance assessment given by the witness and also the absence of a line of sight, as he testified. Mr. Ierace, may I ask you, would you have on other subjects -- I could, of course, now confer with the Judges, but if you say I have at least 50 minutes on other subjects to deal with, then we could do it after we adjourn and inform you perhaps immediately afterwards and not to interrupt the audience now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Mundis, will commence cross-examination. We don't think that he will take much time, perhaps 15 minutes. There is a practical problem with showing the CDs to the witness from this courtroom. Quite simply, we can't. We don't have the equipment here to do it. So that would have to wait until tomorrow anyway. So if we finish, say, in 15 minutes, and we have nothing else to do for the remainder of the day, perhaps we could adjourn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will consider if we can give you an answer or not. So you start now and we will see how far we come and we will either give you some guidance or either inform you that you will get it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. My case manager and I will swap positions, taken that I can see all three Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anyone in the public gallery? No. I think just for leading the witness into the courtroom -- okay. You may escort the witness into the courtroom and then open the curtains again. If there is no one in the public gallery and if it is just for the two seconds that the witness comes in the door to that place, if the Defence would agree that we don't let them down first, which takes quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this matter arises only occasionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Piletta-Zanin, especially since facial distortion is the prevailing protection of the Defence witnesses. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to the first time that you met with the Defence lawyers in this case, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It was around May, April or May, that was the first time. I met Mrs. Prodanovic. I met her in August of this year. I saw her for a very short period of time, and later on, it was in September, I met both lawyers, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me try to clarify. You say in April or May was the fist time. That was April or May of 1990 -- excuse me, April or May of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. In 2002, I spoke to Mrs. Prodanovic a couple of times, and then I confirmed that I would be testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you met again with Mrs. Prodanovic in August of 2002; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Not in August. In August I met the lawyer for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which lawyer or lawyers did you meet in August 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: With Mrs. -- Well, I can't remember her name at the moment. But with the lawyer who is here, with Mara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you first met with Mrs. Prodanovic in April or May of 2002, what did you talk to her about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I met Ms. Pilipovic in August for the first time. And in April and May, it was the first time I spoke over the phone a couple of times with Mrs. Prodanovic. But I spoke to Ms. Pilipovic twice, the first time was in August and it was for half an hour at the most. And in September with -- I spoke to Mrs. Pilipovic and Mr. -- The lawyer, and the conversation lasted for 10 or 15 minutes in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "Mr. The lawyer," are you referring to Mr. Piletta-Zanin who is in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, when was the first time that you discussed the substance of your testimony with either Mr. Piletta-Zanin or Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: With Mrs. Pilipovic, in August 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during that time you say that you spoke for half an hour at the most; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a meeting perhaps here in The Hague where you met with either Mrs. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin for a period of time longer than half an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: On several occasions in The Hague, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did you first arrive here in The Hague, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not really an objection, but I am wondering what the relevance is. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, Mr. Mundis, that you're dealing with a procedural issue, that is, case preparation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and it goes to the issues that Mr. Ierace was addressing the Trial Chamber about immediately prior to the entry of the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed. There was one question that was not answered by the witness, one of your first questions in this line. The witness gave a different -- gave an answer not to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I intended to try to get back to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, again, when was the -- when did you first arrive here in The Hague prior to your testimony in this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I arrived in The Hague on Thursday, was it the 10th or the 11th or perhaps earlier. But it was Thursday, a couple of weeks ago. That's when I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that you've been here almost two weeks; is that right, Witness? This Thursday will be two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How many times since you've been here have you met with either Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Three or four times for about one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say, Witness, "for about one hour," is that one hour on each of those three or four occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the approximately three to four hours in total that you met with Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do you recall the subject matter of your discussions with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, we mostly discussed what I have testified about here today, and I was above all interested in protection measures. And then we discussed what I knew and what I could remember from the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether they showed you any maps or photographs as part of that preparation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you testified earlier this afternoon about having night goggles for nocturnal observation. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes. But they are not goggles. It is infrared -- these infrared binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were these infrared binoculars issued to you by someone in the SRK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I received the binoculars in the brigade, it was issued to me by the brigade. But I don't know where the infrared binoculars came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if other soldiers in your unit were issued with infrared binoculars or received infrared binoculars from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: During that period, the first half of 1993, I was an operations officer and my task was to collect intelligence, to gather intelligence about the enemy. As part of those duties I had a department for reconnaissance department. We were issued with the infrared binoculars which were used for nocturnal observation, in order to gather information on the enemy. I wasn't the only one to use the binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were infrared binoculars common among the troops in your unit or brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: That was the -- those were the only binoculars as far as I know, and there was only that one department, that squad which was under my command in order to gather information on the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the technical specifications of these infrared binoculars that you used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No, not with the technical specification, but I, myself, used these binoculars. And I think that it served its purpose. It could be used for nocturnal observation, to observe the positions at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know about the magnification powers of these binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No, I don't. But I do know that a physical -- it was 50 or 60 centimetres, the diametre was 50 or 60 centimetres, the diametre of the lens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were the infrared binoculars effective? In other words, could you see things at night-time with the infrared binoculars that you could not see with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that the diametre of the lens was 50 or 60 centimetres. Is that correct or was that a translation error?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think that the physical diametre of the entire device was between 50 and 60 centimetres. It was quite bulky. It wasn't easy to handle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long were the infrared binoculars that you used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Well, a metre, I think, a whole metre, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were these infrared binoculars -- did you hold them in your hand or were they mounted on some kind of a tripod or other stabilising device? How did you actually use these binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: It had a sort of mount. We would place it in a certain position and you could observe through them for 5 to 10 minutes and then have a break and then do the same again, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did these infrared binoculars have some kind of power source? Were they powered by batteries or a generator? How did they obtain their power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think it had a battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how heavy the infrared binoculars, including the battery or battery pack, do you recall how heavy these binoculars were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Over 10 or 15 kilos for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In addition to the intelligence gathering that you used the infrared binoculars for, do you know if these infrared binoculars were also used for purposes of target acquisition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if these infrared binoculars were ever used in conjunction with active combat, during periods of active combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No. I performed these duties for six months and it was always with me in my squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you testified that you never saw any snipers among the men that were in your unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, at any time, see within the area of your zone of responsibility any rifles with scopes on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see any soldiers who had personal hunting rifles with them on your side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have just a couple of other areas of questioning I would like to go into and it might perhaps be done in private session, assuming that there is no one in the public gallery. Otherwise, we'd need to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it since you wanted to show photographs to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I will be naming some individuals and I believe the witness might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that could be done in private session, I take it. One of the problems is that I cannot see whether someone enters the public gallery because my view, my line of sight is obstructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I am getting a thumbs up by the guard by the door I think there is no one in the public gallery, so perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. We will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us what was the objective of the Bosnian Serb offensive known as Lukavac 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I know about the part that I was involved in and this was the direction of attack Golo Brdo, 850 elevation point, Orlic and further on towards Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you understand that there were other objectives at the same time outside the area of the confrontation line which was relevant to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Only stories that from the other side there was a second group coming. But where I was involved and where I was at was the direction that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I come back to the benefit of Bosnian Serbs who crossed the confrontation line as a source of intelligence. You told us that you met your first person of that category in mid-1993. Did you understand that other intelligence officers interviewed such people, whenever they crossed the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I suppose you would have been especially interested in such civilians who came from the area opposite your section of the front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were such people interviewed in 1993 either by yourself or intelligence officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I didn't interview them, but certainly they were interviewed. I know that, and if such a person appeared anywhere in the corps, and if this person had been at Zuc, then that person would come to our brigade to give the information they had. So security officers and other operations officer would take the information from that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you understand that there were civilians living in the Kobilja Glava area, that is, on the ABiH side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I am reiterating: For six months, I did this job. Nocturnal observation of the -- observation of the entire sector of the Vogosca Brigade. And it was on the fingers of one hand that you can count the men, including the troops and the civilians. Anyone that I managed to see on that side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Apart from your own observations, did you understand from the Bosnian Serbs who crossed the line that there were civilians living in Kobilja Glava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I believe that they were, but again, I am saying, in the area of responsibility, I gathered data. I was never able to see anyone ever. We presumed that they had trenches from Kosevo, from the city, up to Betanija and all along the line, further on. It was very rare that you were able to even see a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you also understand that there were civilians living in Dumaca in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I can't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say you can't believe that did you ever receive any information from your superiors that there were not civilians living in Dumaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I took part in gathering the data for those four, five, six months until the beginning of July 1993. I intensively worked on gathering the data and observing exactly this terrain, this area of Zuc, Hotonj, up to Kobilja Glava. And it was very rarely that I saw anyone at all in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As an intelligence officer, and with the assistance of the technology you've told us about, were you at least interested to know if there were civilians living in the area opposite your section of the front line, at Kobilja Glava and Dumaca; yes or no? Were you interested or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I suppose one way to find out would have been to ask the United Nations' officials who were in Sarajevo in 1993; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Probably, that was one of the ways, but I was not in a position nor was I so high up in the ranks so as to do something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You have told us that you commanded a company of in excess of some 200 soldiers. Did you ever give them any orders about the targeting of civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Ye. But in the area of Zuc where there was the area of responsibility of my company, there were no civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What were the orders that you gave them in relation to the targeting of civilians in Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I received orders from the command of the brigade that civilians are not to be targeted, that ammunition is to be spared, and that's what I forwarded and told my fighters, my soldiers. Although, because of the area where we held our positions, in this sector there were no civilians. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were the orders that you received as to the targeting of civilians in writing or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: While I was the commanding officer of the company, there were no written orders on the level of the brigade command down to the commanding officers of the companies. There were only verbal orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you give your subordinates any assistance in order to determine whether someone they saw on the other side was to be regarded as a civilian or a combatant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Of course. He is not in uniform, if he doesn't have any weapons, he was considered a civilian, and if he is more than 300 metres away from the line. If he is on the first front line, then he is a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "the first front line" do you mean the very first line of defence of the enemy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown, Mr. President, the Defence exhibit which is the map which has a number "9" on it. I am not sure what the exhibit number was. I think it was part of -- excuse me. I think it is 1793. Whilst that is being prepared --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is that the map that refers to sniping incident 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry, 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the area of Kobilja Glava, was there a mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The mosque was destroyed during the war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think it was. I don't recall whether it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The mosque -- withdraw that. Would you please look at the map alongside you and could you please point to number 14, that is the red dot with number 14 alongside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, the position of the mosque in relation to that dot was to the south-east; is that correct? South-east, not north-east.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I think -- I think it would be in this area, that the mosque was in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates to the left of the name in capital letters of Kobilja Glava in the vicinity of a yellow line which has written on it "Kobilja Glava."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there is a new mosque there these days, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't go into that part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you said earlier you think the mosque was destroyed, I suggest to you the mosque was shelled by forces of the Bosnian-Serb Army. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Never. There was never a single order that was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object with regard to chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if my learned colleague means by that whether it was inside or outside the indictment period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how I understand the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, at this stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Chronology -- I mean, chronology could mean a lot of things, but -- are you objecting because it is irrelevant because it is outside the time frame of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that I know from what we have heard from other testimonies that this happened at the other time period from the one that is covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your answer was yes. Mr. Ierace, would you respond to it in the presence of the witness or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the questions I have put have deliberately not referred to the time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Our enquiries continue in relation to this fresh subject and I submit it has relevance even though it isn't linked to a particular time period, other than during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question now has been answered. Do you intend to proceed on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Look at the map alongside you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes Mr. President, it's an objection that I made. The Prosecutor has to know which period he is talking about, and not ask questions if he knows that this is outside of the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He will not pursue the matter. The question has been answered already. That's what happens now and then as all parties know. And Mr. Ierace now moves to his next subject, apart from that it is two minutes to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That will be enough time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That will be enough time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the map alongside you there appears a long black rectangle. Please point to it. No.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Was that building a, during the war, the subject of shelling by Bosnian-Serb Army forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP14
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before the war, was it some sort of medical facility, perhaps a teaching facility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same point, the same problem, Mr. President, that would it be possible to specify exactly. Are you talking before September 1992 or not? I believe that the Prosecution has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution does not have to say. The relevance of these questions go to the identification of the building. You may remember, Mr. President some evidence from various Prosecution witnesses as to the nature of that building. I seek to confirm that with this witness, and I think he has already done it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that it is not mainly the shelling, but the character of the building that you are seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But perhaps I could press that answer because there isn't an answer in the transcript. That's the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this in dispute, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? I mean, there was a question about the character of the building. Is the character of the building in dispute taking into consideration that some evidence has been led?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as far as the type of the building is concerned, no, but I don't see why we would be talking about the shelling and regarding the building. We can also speak about the cathedral and speak about the shelling separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That has to do with the appearance of the building, Mr. President. If one has seen that building, it is an obvious feature which helps to identify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I do understand that the character of the building is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, in that case, Mr. President, that completes my questions, subject to the ruling from the Trial Chamber. If it was possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine you would rather know it now than tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Since we are sitting tomorrow afternoon, Mr. President, if we could be informed by the Senior Legal Officer in chambers perhaps during the course of the morning. That would assist us in what preparations we make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About the two issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say in the course of the morning or do you mean in the course of the evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think we sit from 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are sitting in the afternoon tomorrow morning. And that would be timely enough for --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, very briefly. If I understand it well, what happens is that Mr. Ierace is asking you to intervene on the basis of an assessment, anticipated assessment of evidence. And to the Defence it seems extremely dangerous to do this sort of thing, because we are just at the beginning of the presentation of our case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Judges will discuss the matter. We will adjourn until tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. Is it the same courtroom? Courtroom II, so we have all the technical facilities, if we would need them, we would have them available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
